title: Quant-profile gating and calibration-driven kernel scheduler for mixed-precision inference
creator: Priya Rao
description: Goal: Implement a kernel scheduling layer that uses per-model quantization profiles (FP8/INT8) and calibration metadata to pick an execution path at request time. The scheduler must: 1) read a compact quant_profile manifest (calibration ranges, per-op sensitivity scores, preferred kernels), 2) gate between FP16/FP8/INT8 kernels based on accuracy budget and latency/cost constraints, and 3) provide deterministic fallback logic when a chosen kernel path is not available for a target hardware. Motivation: past incidents showed fallback paths can blow up latency or silently degrade output quality when profiling is stale. This ticket scopes design + implementation of the gating rules, runtime config surface, and the calibration validation harness to verify accuracy/regressions across quant profiles.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can select an FP8 or INT8 kernel based on a model's quant_profile manifest and per-request accuracy budget (SLO parameter).
Runtime emits an explainability header in logs for each decision: selected_path, profile_id, reason (latency/cost/accuracy/fallback).
Offline calibration harness generates per-layer sensitivity and a single-profile artifact that the scheduler can consume (schema JSON).
End-to-end accuracy regression tests run in CI and flag >0.5% top-level perplexity delta (or configured threshold) for any quantized path compared to FP16 baseline.
Canary rollout: 1% traffic routed to new gating logic for two weeks with no customer-impact incidents; metrics stable in telemetry dashboards.
technical_design: Design Highlights: - Quant_profile manifest: model_id, profile_id, version, per-op scale/zero-point ranges, sensitivity score (0-1), prefer_kernel list (hw_tag->kernel_name), fallback_order. - Decision logic: compute a per-request 'accuracy budget' derived from request headers or route defaults. Score each candidate path by estimated delta (from sensitivity), latency cost (micro-benchmarks keyed by hw_tag), and monetary unit-cost. Use a weighted score: score = alpha*estimated_delta + beta*latency_ms + gamma*cost. Choose lowest score under accuracy_budget constraint. - Calibration workflow: offline dataset -> per-layer calibration -> compute sensitivity and recommended quant scheme (FP8 vs INT8) -> validate on validation set -> produce profile artifact with checksums. - Runtime: load profiles lazily; allow hot-reload via config API; attach profile checksum to logs/traces. - Fallbacks: if preferred kernel missing, try next in fallback_order; if hardware unsupported, route to remote-hosted fallback pool (Dedicated/hosted) with traceable cost tags.
performance_targets: Quantized FP8 path latency within 1.2x of FP16 for 2k token sequences on A100/RTX-class hardware.
INT8 path should improve token throughput by >=1.6x vs FP16 for batched generation under steady state.
Decision overhead: scheduling logic adds <150 microseconds to per-request latency in hot path.
Memory overhead for loaded profiles: <5% RAM increase per model on serving node.
testing_plan: Unit tests for scheduler scoring and fallback logic (edge cases: missing profile, expired version, corrupted checksum).
Integration tests in CI: spin up runtime with synthetic HW tags and verify chosen kernels align with offline predictions.
Calibration validation: run quantized model candidate vs FP16 baseline on held-out eval set and produce detailed layer-wise delta report.
Distributed canary: Gradual rollout scripts and monitoring alerts (per-route perplexity, latency p95, token cost); automatic rollback threshold defined.
Chaos test: Simulate kernel unavailability and verify fallback to remote pool with correct billing/tags.
rollout_strategy: Start with internal-only models and a small set of models marked 'alpha-quant' in model registry. Canary at 1% customer traffic for 14 days, then 10%, then full rollout after metrics plateau and no regressions. Use feature-flag gated config and ability to pin model->force_fp16. We will include an opt-out label for customers who require byte-for-byte determinism.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: stale calibration profiles produce quality regressions. Mitigation: include profile versioning + TTL and mandatory offline re-calibration pipeline triggered after model re-training.
Risk: hardware kernel mismatch. Mitigation: maintain micro-benchmark matrix per hw_tag and fail-open to FP16 with telemetry and alerting.
Risk: decision overhead hurts ultra-low-latency routes. Mitigation: precompute routing table for common model/hw/sequence-length buckets and use fast-path cache in serving process.
